burdens.title: consultants and advisory teams should not spend their best hours rebuilding context.

items.label: Context
items.title: Client context changes every week
items.description: New interviews, documents, and sponsor feedback change the working picture faster than a static brief can capture it.

items.label: Format
items.title: Research is difficult to trace
items.description: Claims get copied into working documents while the original interview, report, or calculation becomes difficult to recover.

items.label: Coordination
items.title: Analysis and slides drift apart
items.description: The analysis may change after the exhibit is built, leaving recommendations, numbers, and presentation pages out of sync.

items.label: Continuity
items.title: Each engagement repeats setup work

buildingBlocks.title: Compose the workflow from practical building blocks.
buildingBlocks.description: Floatboat does not prescribe one professional method. It follows the materials, standards, and approval points you select.

items.example: Start from approved files, records, and sources rather than an empty prompt.
Classify material, normalize names, and identify missing inputs.
Pull facts, dates, data, claims, and open questions.
Contrast versions, standards, periods, or alternatives.
items.result: A focused list of changes and differences.

items.example: Turn approved material into briefs, outlines, tables, and drafts.
Save proven steps, formats, and approval points.
items.result: A reusable workflow shaped by the team.

workflows.title: Start from real assignments, not a fixed professional playbook.
workflows.description: Each workflow begins with material and rules you control, returns an inspectable result, and stops before professional judgment.

items.title: Turn discovery into a working brief
items.job: Consolidate interviews, documents, constraints, and open questions before the team commits to an approach.
items.output: A client-context brief with open questions and source links.
items.boundary: Consultants validate what the client meant and decide the engagement direction.

items.title: Build an evidence-backed recommendation
items.job: Connect research findings to hypotheses, alternatives, and implications without losing the source trail.
items.output: An evidence matrix, option set, and recommendation narrative.
items.boundary: The consulting team owns assumptions, analysis quality, and final advice.

items.title: Prepare a workshop or executive deck
items.job: Transform approved analysis into a coherent session plan, exhibit list, and editable presentation structure.
items.output: A workshop pack or executive-ready deck outline.
items.boundary: A consultant approves claims, tone, and every client-facing deliverable.

boundaries.title: Automate preparation, not professional responsibility.
boundaries.description: The useful boundary is between preparing an inspectable work product and making a consequential professional decision.
assists: Source indexes, context briefs, and evidence maps
Comparisons, extracted fields, and open questions
Meeting packs, status summaries, and communication drafts
Grounded outlines, reports, and editable first drafts
retains: Verification of facts, data, and sources
Approval for every external publication, submission, or consequential action
boundaries.note: Floatboat is a general-purpose Agent Workspace. It does not replace professional qualification, legal responsibility, or organizational governance. Data handling depends on the models, tools, connectors, permissions, and policies selected for the workspace.

faq.title: AI workspace questions for consultants and advisory teams
faq.description: Consulting teams need to preserve source trails, adapt to changing client context, and keep recommendations accountable to the people presenting them.

items.question: Is Floatboat a consulting methodology or project-management system?
items.answer: No. It is a workspace for executing the research, synthesis, drafting, and coordination steps around an engagement. Your team still chooses the methodology, workplan, governance, and system of record.

items.question: Can it produce a client recommendation on its own?
items.answer: It can connect supplied evidence to hypotheses and draft alternatives, but consultants must test assumptions, resolve contradictions, weigh trade-offs, and own the advice presented to a client.

items.question: Can each engagement use its own templates and terminology?
items.answer: Yes. A workspace can begin from the client brief, interview guide, issue tree, exhibit conventions, and review cadence selected for that engagement.

items.question: How do we keep a recommendation tied to evidence?
items.answer: Maintain source links beside claims, distinguish client statements from external evidence, expose unresolved assumptions, and have the workstream owner verify every number and conclusion before it reaches a deck.

items.question: How should confidential client material be handled?
items.answer: Follow the engagement's confidentiality terms and firm policy, separate workspaces where appropriate, grant only necessary access, and review the data handling of every selected model, tool, and connector.

items.question: Will drafts go directly to the client?
items.answer: Not in the recommended setup. Workshop packs, executive summaries, emails, and decks remain editable drafts until the engagement team approves the evidence, language, recipients, and release.

items.question: Where should a consulting team start?
items.answer: Use one completed discovery cycle: provide approved interview notes and background documents, generate a source-linked working brief, and compare it with what the team would normally prepare by hand.

finalCta.title: Give the repetitive preparation around consultants and advisory teams a better workspace.
finalCta.description: Start with one engagement question, its approved evidence, and the next client deliverable. Keep the source trail visible while the recommendation takes shape.
